title: Solar System Scope planet textures (2K, equirectangular)
source: https://www.solarsystemscope.com/textures/ (mirrored on Wikimedia Commons, Category:Solar System Scope)
credit: Textures by Solar System Scope (solarsystemscope.com), based on NASA imagery, CC BY 4.0
notes: 2048x1024 equirectangular maps for three.js/WebGL spheres or flat "planet cards". 4K/8K versions exist upstream (see docs/ASSET_CATALOG.md). `2k_saturn_ring_alpha.png` is the ring strip (2048x125, alpha).

title: NASA 3D Resources planet maps
license: Public domain / NASA media usage guidelines (no attribution required, NASA logo rules apply)
notes: Lower resolution than the Solar System Scope set (720x360 to 1440x720) but public domain, useful when attribution-free assets are required. TIFF originals exist upstream.

title: NASA SVS CGI Moon Kit (LRO colour map + displacement)
credit: NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio (Ernie Wright); LRO LROC WAC / LOLA data
notes: The definitive Moon (Chandra) texture. 4K/8K/16K TIFF colour maps and 16-bit displacement maps are available at the SVS page for high-end rendering.

title: ESO Milky Way 360 panorama (Serge Brunier)
notes: Equirectangular all-sky photograph; ideal as a sky-sphere or hero background. Original 6000x3000 TIFF upstream.

title: NASA 3D Resources star maps (Tycho, Hipparcos, Yale Bright Star)
credit: NASA / Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio
notes: Equirectangular star-field maps (celestial coordinates) for sky spheres and dark backgrounds.

title: Poly Haven night-sky HDRI (tonemapped JPG, downscaled to 4K)
credit: Poly Haven (Greg Zaal et al.), CC0
notes: Real night-sky panoramas with Milky Way and horizon; equirectangular 4096x2048. Full HDR (up to 24K EXR) upstream.

title: NASA hero photographs of the grahas (Sun, Moon, planets, eclipses)
credit: NASA / JPL-Caltech / GSFC / SDO / Cassini / Voyager / MESSENGER / Mariner teams
notes: One iconic photograph per graha for splash/hero panels: Surya (SDO), Chandra (LRO full moon), Mangala (Viking, Valles Marineris), Budha (MESSENGER), Guru (Cassini), Shukra (Mariner 10), Shani (Cassini), Rahu/Ketu (eclipse composites), plus Uranus, Neptune and Earthrise. Downscaled to max 2048px; originals via images.nasa.gov.

title: Navagraha paintings, manuscripts and sculpture (Wikimedia Commons, museum releases)
source: https://commons.wikimedia.org (Cleveland Museum of Art CC0, LACMA PD, Walters CC0, Hermitage PD, Wellcome CC BY, private CC0 uploads)
license: Mixed: Public domain / CC0 / CC BY 4.0 / CC BY-SA 4.0 — see per-file table
credit: Per file; see table (museum credit lines in the Commons file pages)
notes: Museum-quality source imagery for graha portraits, backgrounds and "authentic" texture (manuscript pages of the Prasnapradipa, a Brihajjataka manuscript, a Peshwa horoscope). Downloaded at 1280px; originals up to 6000px on Commons.

title: E. A. Rodrigues, "The Complete Hindoo Pantheon" (1842) — the nine grahas, one plate each
credit: E. A. Rodrigues, The Complete Hindoo Pantheon, 1842 (public domain), via Wikimedia Commons
notes: The only stylistically consistent public-domain set of all nine graha deities found on the open web: Surya, Chandra, Mangala (Angaraka), Budha, Brihaspati, Shukra, Shani, Rahu, Ketu. Hand-coloured lithographs, suitable for graha cards after background clean-up.

title: Wellcome Collection Indian astrological prints and paintings
license: Public Domain Mark / CC BY 4.0 (Wellcome Collection)
notes: The Barlow engraving is the single best "nakshatra symbol" reference plate found: 28 lunar mansions incl. Abhijit, each with its emblem and Devanagari label. Fetched at 1600px via IIIF; full resolution via https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/image/<id>/full/full/0/default.jpg

title: Stellarium "Indian Vedic" sky culture (rashi + nakshatra constellations with illustrations)
credit: Tanmoy Saha, Vishvas Vasuki and the sanskrit-coders community; re-worked by Susanne M. Hoffmann (Stellarium)
notes: index.json holds 49 constellations (12 rashi, 27 nakshatra, extras) as HIP star-ID line lists plus image anchors (star → pixel) so each illustration can be placed on a star map. Illustrations are simple clip-art style; treat as placeholders or trace them into a house style.

title: Stellarium "Indian (Nakshatras)" sky culture — 28 nakshatra sketches
credit: Susanne M. Hoffmann (with B. S. Shylaja), Stellarium
notes: One small (about 210px) coloured sketch per nakshatra (1 Ashvini … 27 Revati + 28 Abhijit) with star anchors in index.json; description.md contains a short, scholarly text for every nakshatra. Low resolution: use for reference or as a base for redrawing.

title: d3-celestial star map library + sky data (stars to mag 6, constellations, Milky Way, planets)
credit: Olaf Frohn, d3-celestial (BSD-3-Clause); data derived from HYG, Stellarium and IAU sources (see data/readme.md)
notes: Everything needed for an in-browser sky chart: ecliptic/equatorial grids, zodiac band, Milky Way outline, 27 nakshatra boundaries can be drawn as 13°20′ ecliptic sectors on top. stars.8.json (5 MB) and stars.14.json (15 MB) are upstream if deeper zoom is needed.

title: Stellarium sky-cultures repo: nakshatra star-line data (28 nakshatras as HIP IDs)
credit: Tanmoy Saha, Vishvas Vasuki, sanskrit-coders community; Susanne M. Hoffmann (Stellarium)
notes: Lines-only variant (no images) of the Indian sky culture; western.index.json included for the IAU constellation lines + image anchors (Johan Meuris art, Free Art License, not bundled).

title: Zodiac Fonts — free tier (55 astrological SVG glyphs + WOFF2 icon font)
notes: Clean currentColor SVGs: 12 signs, 11 planets, North/South Node (Rahu/Ketu), Lilith, Chiron, 12 houses + ASC/MC, 8 lunar phases, 5 major aspects, retrograde. Also shipped as a PUA icon font (see glyphs.json for code points).

title: Astromoony — astronomical symbol font with per-glyph SVG sources
notes: Maps real Unicode code points (U+2609 Sun, U+263D Moon, U+263F–2647 planets, U+2BD3 Pluto alt…). SVG files are named by code point. No zodiac signs or nodes; pair with Noto Sans Symbols for those.

title: Astronomicon astrological font (Roberto Corona)
credit: Astronomicon by Roberto Corona, SIL OFL 1.1
notes: 192 glyphs mapped onto ASCII letters/digits (planets, signs, aspects, asteroids, Uranian points). Open preview/index.html to see the key map rendered; the font is designed to blend with modern UI type.

title: HamburgSymbols astrological font (Uranian / general glyphs)
license: Public domain (embedded font notice: "HamburgSymbols is Public Domain (2005)")
notes: 226 glyphs on ASCII positions; includes planets, signs, aspects and the eight Hamburg-school hypothetical planets.

title: StarFont Sans / Serif astrological fonts (Anthony I. P. Owen)
license: Public domain (released by the author, see StarFont.txt)
credit: StarFont by Anthony I. P. Owen, packaged by Matthew Skala (public domain)
notes: Classic 1993 astrological glyph fonts in two styles; the name table is minimal so some tools show no family name.

title: AstroChart (Kibo) glyph SVGs incl. Hershey stroke sets
notes: Single-stroke (Hershey) glyphs are perfect for plotter-style / engraved looks and animate well with stroke-dashoffset. The upstream files are Inkscape A4 pages with the glyph drawn small; here the root viewBox was rewritten to the content bounding box (path geometry untouched) so they display at full size.

title: VedAstro UI icons: 9 graha icons, 30 tithi Moon phases, 12 rashi event icons, zodiac wheel
notes: The only MIT-licensed set found with explicit Rahu and Ketu icons. Caveat: the nine graha icons are cartoon planets with the English name badge baked into the SVG ("JUPITER", "KETU"…) and Rahu/Ketu are recoloured crescents, so they need editing before production use. Strong parts: moon-1.svg … moon-30.svg are photographic-style Moon renders for the 30 tithis (Shukla 1 → Krishna 15); the 12 rashi "event" icons are constellation stick-figures; zodiac-360.svg is a full zodiac wheel; north-chart-source.svg / south-chart-source.svg are editable North- and South-Indian chart templates.

title: Tabler Icons — zodiac + celestial subset (outline and filled)
credit: Tabler Icons by Paweł Kuna, MIT
notes: 24px grid, 2px stroke; the 12 zodiac icons match the rest of the UI icon language.

title: Weather Icons (Erik Flowers) — 28+28 Moon phase glyphs, sun, eclipses, clock faces
credit: Weather Icons by Erik Flowers (SIL OFL 1.1); artwork by Lukas Bischoff
notes: 28 phase steps ≈ one glyph per tithi (the 30 tithis map onto 28 with two doublings); the "alt" set draws the lit portion as a disc.

title: Meteocons (Bas Milius) — animated + static Moon phases, Sun, stars, eclipse, in 4 styles
notes: Animated SVGs use embedded CSS/SMIL, no JS. Styles: fill (colour), flat, line, monochrome. Great for a living Panchanga header (moon phase, sunrise/sunset, hora clock).

credit: Sri Yantra generator by Vibz.Art, MIT

title: Astronomy Engine (Don Cross) — Sun/Moon/planet positions, phases, rise/set, eclipses; single browser file

notes: ±1 arcminute, no data files, 116 KB — enough for a standalone HTML panchanga/kundali (tropical → sidereal via ayanamsa; lunar nodes via SearchMoonNode or a mean-node formula). Swiss-Ephemeris-grade alternatives are listed in the catalog.
